SIGN.note: 6x3-k3 is the sole carrier where depthless SIGN fails, with one contradiction; depth parity repairs it.

SIGNED_PARITY.note: The coarsest point in the entire frozen role/depth grid is exact on every hard carrier.

findings.statement: Exact canonical C role identity is unnecessary in the common scalar carrier: C_ROLELESS is sufficient at the minimal exact grid point for both SIGN and SIGNED_PARITY.
Exact D0/D1 depth identity is unnecessary in both common realizations. SIGN needs only depth parity; SIGNED_PARITY needs no depth index at all.
Under SIGNED_PARITY, C_ROLELESS+D_DEPTHLESS is scalar-exact on all three hard carriers and is the coarsest point of the frozen role/depth partial order.
On 4x5-k4 the SIGNED_PARITY roleless/depthless quotient reduces structural image rank from 282 to 262 while preserving the full two-dimensional scalar dependency image.
For plain SIGN, depthless exchange is already exact on 4x5-k4 and 6x3-k4 but leaves one contradiction on 6x3-k3; retaining only depth parity closes that final gap.

The most compact common tested exchange representation no longer names component width, capacity roles, or depth levels. It retains only signed bucket counts for capacity changes and the two owner-separated depth-change channels.
